qs.q: Which specific serotypes of Adenovirus are responsible for causing Acute Respiratory Disease (ARD), characterized by fever, cough, and pharyngitis, particularly in close contact settings like military barracks?
qs.e: Serotypes 4 and 7 are associated with Acute Respiratory Disease and can be targeted with live oral vaccines in military recruits. Serotypes 40 through 42 are instead known to cause infant gastroenteritis.
qs.s: Adenovirus & Parvovirus B19: Non-Enveloped DNA Virus Guide: MCQs

qs.q: An outbreak of acute respiratory disease occurs among military recruits living in crowded barracks. Laboratory analysis identifies a double-stranded DNA, non-enveloped icosahedral virus known for its resistance to drying and ability to spread via fomites. What is the causative agent?
qs.e: Adenovirus is a non-enveloped dsDNA virus that resists drying and frequently causes acute respiratory disease in crowded settings like military camps. Influenza and RSV are RNA enveloped viruses susceptible to environmental drying.

ai.subject: Microbiology & immunology
ai.summary: Acute Respiratory Disease (ARD) is a bacterial infection, most often caused by Haemophilus influenzae serotypes 4 and 7, that presents with fever, cough, pharyngitis and cervical adenitis, especially in crowded settings such as military recruits.

sections.p: ARD is an acute bacterial infection of the upper airway that spreads rapidly in close‑contact groups. It is distinct from common cold viruses and from pertussis, though symptoms overlap.
b: Peak incidence in young adults in crowded environments
Self‑limited in healthy hosts, but can progress to pneumonia

sections.p: Haemophilus influenzae is a small Gram‑negative coccobacillus requiring X (hemin) and V (NAD) factors for growth. Serotypes 4 and 7 possess a polysaccharide capsule that enhances virulence.
b: Capsular serotypes 4 & 7 most associated with ARD
Non‑typeable strains cause otitis media and sinusitis
Beta‑lactamase production common, causing ampicillin resistance

sections.p: The organism spreads by respiratory droplets and direct contact with contaminated secretions. Colonisation of the nasopharynx precedes invasion of the pharyngeal mucosa.
b: Crowded living quarters increase droplet exposure
Transient carriage in healthy adults is common
No environmental reservoir outside the human host

sections.p: ARD presents with fever, sore throat, dry cough, and tender cervical lymphadenopathy. Complications include bronchitis, pneumonia, and, rarely, sepsis.
b: Cervical adenitis distinguishes it from viral pharyngitis
Progression to lower respiratory tract disease in immunocompromised patients

sections.p: Diagnosis relies on clinical pattern plus laboratory confirmation when available. In low‑resource settings, treatment may be empirical based on presentation.

t.a: Throat swab culture on chocolate agar with X/V factors
t.b: Identifies H. influenzae and serotype; positive culture confirms bacterial cause

t.a: PCR for H. influenzae DNA from respiratory secretions
t.b: Rapid detection when culture unavailable; a positive result supports ARD
Leukocytosis with neutrophil predominance suggests bacterial infection; normal WBC does not exclude ARD

sections.p: First‑line therapy targets the organism while supportive care manages symptoms. Prevention focuses on hygiene and vaccination where available.
b: Use a third‑generation cephalosporin (e.g., cefotaxime) for beta‑lactamase‑producing strains; avoids ampicillin failure
Macrolides are alternatives in penicillin‑allergic patients; avoid tetracyclines in children
Hydration, antipyretics, and rest are essential supportive measures
Isolation of cases in crowded settings limits spread

sections.p: Key points to remember for exams and clinical practice.
b: Serotypes 4 & 7 are classic for ARD in military recruits
Cervical adenitis with fever‑cough‑pharyngitis points to H. influenzae, not pertussis

whenToSeekHelp: Rapidly worsening cough or difficulty breathing
Signs of sepsis: hypotension, confusion, tachycardia

faq.q: How is ARD different from pertussis?
faq.a: ARD has a short cough and prominent cervical adenitis; pertussis shows a prolonged paroxysmal cough with whooping.

faq.q: Can a viral infection cause the same symptoms?
faq.a: Viruses cause sore throat and cough but rarely produce tender cervical nodes or the rapid progression to pneumonia seen in ARD.

faq.q: Is there a vaccine for ARD?
faq.a: No specific vaccine for serotypes 4/7 exists; routine Hib vaccine covers type b, not the ARD serotypes.
